## Symptom

After a global model-spec / tier-menu fix lands (an owner or agent runs
`config:tiers-set` to replace a broken/renamed spec, e.g. dropping a dead
`claude-sonnet-5[1m]:high` for `sonnet[1m]`), a specific pot's `cup`/`kettle`
spawns **keep dying on "selected model unavailable/inaccessible"** — for hours,
long after the global fix is committed and live.

## The trap (why this ate ~4h once — EI-12807)

Every escalation in the chain assumed the **launcher/orchestrator hadn't
reloaded the fix** and chased a restart. It had reloaded. The real cause:

- A pot can carry its OWN `pot:set-steering { modelTiers, modelOverrides }`
  SESSION override.
- **Per-pot steering ALWAYS wins over the workspace default, by design.**
- So a `config:tiers-set` fix to the *workspace* menu **cannot reach** a pot
  that pins the old spec through its own steering. The stale pin silently
  survives the fix and keeps every spawn on that pot pinned to a dead model.

A stale pin like `claude-sonnet-5[1m]:high` is extra sneaky: it passes
`validateCloudModelSpec` (it *looks* like a full `claude-…` provider id) and it
is family-identical to the live `sonnet` — so nothing that compares at
family granularity flags it.

## Diagnose it in one read

```
pot:get-steering { pot: '<slug>' }
```

Look at `modelSpecDrift` (added by EI-12807): a **non-empty** array lists the
pinned specs that are no longer in the committed tier menu. Also check
`steering.modelTiers` / `steering.modelOverrides` directly — a pot pinning specs
that don't match your current `config:tiers-get` menu is the smoking gun.

The Mug wake brief now also renders a loud **"Steering pins a DEAD model spec
(EI-12807)"** nudge, so a steered pot surfaces this on its very next wake.

## Fix

Reconcile the pot back to the fixed workspace default:

```
pot:set-steering { pot: '<slug>', modelTiers: null, modelOverrides: null }
```

(Or set fresh, valid specs if the override was intentional.) This clears the
stale per-pot pins so the pot inherits the corrected workspace tier menu.

## General lesson

When a *global* config fix "doesn't take" for one tenant/pot/session, suspect a
**more-specific override that wins over the global default** before you suspect a
reload/restart lag. Precedence layers (session > workspace > committed) are
exactly where a fix at one layer silently fails to reach a pin at a higher one.
